title: Krisp Pricing 2026: Free, Pro, Business Plans Compared
summary: Krisp pricing starts free but caps transcription and notes. Upgrade to Pro for one user, Business for admin controls, or Enterprise for SSO.
body_markdown:
## What Krisp costs at realistic usage


Starting on monthly billing costs you exactly twice what annual billing does, so the price of staying flexible is large and worth knowing before you click.


Per[Voibe's Krisp pricing breakdown](https://www.getvoibe.com/resources/krisp-pricing/) , Core runs $192 a year per user on monthly billing against $96 on annual, which means **you're paying double by choosing monthly** . Advanced runs $360 against $180.


Pay the monthly premium only while you're still testing whether the free plan's cap is the thing stopping you, then switch to annual once the answer is yes.


### Freelancer with a few calls a week


A solo freelancer on Core pays $96 a year on annual billing, or $192 monthly. That's $8 a month at the annual rate per[Getvoibe](https://www.getvoibe.com/resources/krisp-pricing/) .


Stay free until you hit the cap in a real week, then buy Core. Advanced at $180 a year (or $360 monthly) is more than this use needs.


### Remote worker in a noisy room


The paid tiers raise the meeting transcription and notes limits, not noise cancellation, so a remote worker who takes few meetings gains little by upgrading.


If you also run many recorded calls, Core at $96 a year covers it. The jump to Advanced at $180 a year only pays when Core's limits, not your room, are the problem.


### Krisp cost for a team of five


Five seats on Core cost $480 a year on annual billing or $960 monthly, meaning you'd spend **an extra $480 annually for monthly billing** . On Advanced the same team pays $900 annually or $1,800 monthly, an extra $900 yearly if you opt for monthly.


Go annual here: it saves $900 a year on Advanced. If you need admin controls, check which tier holds them before you pay for the cheaper one.


### Krisp limits and fees that surprise buyers


Three things catch buyers. First, the annual discount requires a twelve-month commitment, so $96 only looks cheap if you'll still use the tool next November.


Second, every price above is per user, so a team's bill scales linearly with headcount and five seats means five times the solo figure.


Third, **a paid plan still has usage limits** , so confirm the current caps on[Krisp's own pricing page](https://krisp.ai/) before assuming "paid" means unlimited.
